meta.title: My rough classification of the ACL 2026 papers
meta.dek: I was going through the ACL 2026 papers (Main and Findings) and roughly classified them. The shape I kept seeing: self-improvement crossed over from ML into NLP — self-evolving agents, self-correction, and self-play show up as first-class methods, not gimmicks.
meta.meta_html: Scope: self-improvement, reasoning, agents/RAG, retrieval & ranking, alignment, evaluation, efficiency, multilinguality, multimodal & safety  |  a curated, verified sample — not all 4,400+  |  ↗ Reading list

takeaway: My overall read: the year's throughline is self-improvement. NLP papers stopped treating self-refinement as a prompting trick and started building it into training — self-evolving multi-agent teams, models that correct themselves against solvers and verifiers, and self-play with formal checks. The counter-current: RAG now has to defend against a corpus that is itself model-written.
shifts_heading: Roughly, the papers fell into these groups

shifts.heading: The self-improving agent becomes an ACL topic
shifts.prose: The headline shift: agents and models that improve from their own experience — self-evolving multi-agent teams, fully self-synthetic alignment data, test-time self-training. The frontier question is credit assignment: several of these only work because they pair self-generation with a verification gate before anything is written back.

anchors.title: TT-SI: Self-Improving LLM Agents with Test-Time Training
Aligning Large Language Models via Fully Self-Synthetic Data
Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems via Textual Backpropagation

shifts.heading: Self-correction grows teeth
shifts.prose: Self-correction moved from “ask the model to try again” to structured loops grounded in an external signal — an ASP solver, a formal verifier, a reward model retrained on its own failures. The papers that work share a shape: the correction is checked by something the model cannot just talk its way past.

anchors.title: LLMs as ASP Programmers: Self-Correction Enables Task-Agnostic Nonmonotonic Reasoning
Teach a Reward Model to Correct Itself: Reward Guided Adversarial Failure Discovery
QueueEDIT: Structural Self-Correction for Sequential Model Editing in LLMs

shifts.heading: Self-play and self-reward reach NLP
shifts.prose: Self-play and self-reward, mostly an ML story until now, showed up in language work — a generator/evaluator pair trained against each other under a formal-verification referee, and synthetic rubrics generated to reward-model your own outputs. The open question is the same as in ML: how do you keep the two halves honest.

anchors.title: Improving LLM Code Reasoning via Semantic Equivalence Self-Play with Formal Verification
OpenRubrics: Towards Scalable Synthetic Rubric Generation for Reward Modeling and LLM Alignment
Enhancing Long-Chain Reasoning Distillation through Error-Aware Self-Reflection

shifts.heading: RAG's new worry: the corpus is now model-generated
shifts.prose: A pointed counter-theme: as the web fills with LLM output, retrieval starts eating its own tail. Papers this year detect model-generated contamination in the retrieval corpus, check knowledge-thought coherence in reasoning chains, and stream-detect hallucination as it forms. Faithfulness became an engineering target, not a caveat.

anchors.title: LLM-Generated Text May Harm Your Retrieval! A Robust Detection Strategy for RAG
CheckRLM: Effective Knowledge–Thought Coherence Checking in Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning
Streaming Hallucination Detection in Long Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

shifts.heading: Reward modeling and judging get agentic
shifts.prose: Reward models and judges stopped being frozen scorers. This year they use tools, run curricula, and get benchmarked for their own vulnerability — a verifier that interleaves reasoning with tool calls, curriculum-ordered AI feedback, and writing benchmarks that show LLM-judges buckle under textual perturbation.

anchors.title: AgentV-RL: Scaling Reward Modeling with Agentic Verifier
Curriculum-RLAIF: Curriculum Alignment with Reinforcement Learning from AI Feedback
HoWToBench: Holistic Evaluation for LLM's Writing Capability using Tree of Writing

shifts.heading: Retrieval goes agentic and reasoning-intensive
shifts.prose: IR showed up strongly at ACL this year: retrievers trained for reasoning-intensive queries, agentic search loops optimised with RL, and embedding models rebuilt for reasoning rather than surface match. The recurring benchmark is BRIGHT, and the recurring worry is robustness — several papers defend the retrieval stage against poisoning and style bias.

anchors.title: Agentic-R: Learning to Retrieve for Agentic Search
Rethinking Reasoning-Intensive Retrieval: Evaluating and Advancing Retrievers in Agentic Search Systems
ReasonEmbed: Enhanced Text Embeddings for Reasoning-Intensive Document Retrieval

thread.heading: One quieter thread: multilingual reasoning, done efficiently
thread.html: A steady undercurrent kept pushing multilingual reasoning without blowing up the token budget: Less Languages, Less Tokens ACL (DOI) cuts >50% decoding cost across 18 languages, and LANG ACL (DOI) uses language-adaptive hints so RL doesn't wreck language consistency.

appendix_title: The full list, grouped the way I sorted it
appendix_dek: The ACL 2026 papers I went through, each with a one-line note and its ACL Anthology DOI (arXiv where I could verify a preprint). A curated sample of Main and Findings, not the whole proceedings.

papers.title: TT-SI: Self-Improving LLM Agents with Test-Time Training
papers.note: Adapts an agent on the fly by test-time training on self-augmented uncertain instances: +5.48% accuracy with 68x fewer training samples.

papers.title: Towards Self-Improving Error Diagnosis in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.note: ErrorProbe attributes semantic failures in multi-agent systems and updates memory only after successful verification.

papers.title: Aligning Large Language Models via Fully Self-Synthetic Data
papers.note: SAO generates and self-evaluates all prompts, responses and preferences for alignment with no external data.

papers.title: EVOTOOL: Self-Evolving Tool-Use Policy Optimization via Blame-Aware Mutation and Diversity-Aware Selection
papers.note: Optimizes a modular tool-use policy through a self-evolving loop of trajectory collection, blame attribution and targeted mutation.

papers.title: Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems via Textual Backpropagation
papers.note: Agentic Neural Network: multi-agent teams self-evolve roles, prompts and coordination via a backprop-like backward phase.

papers.title: A Self-Evolving LLM Agent Framework for Role-Based Norm Compliance in Healthcare
papers.note: A healthcare agent with structured memory and dual-layer reflection that updates its prompts via preference-style optimization with AI feedback.

papers.title: AgentFactory: A Self-Evolving Framework Through Executable Subagent Accumulation and Reuse
papers.note: A demo framework whose library of executable subagents grows and improves over time to cut effort on similar tasks.

papers.title: Improving Long-Context Translation via Self-Supervised Dual Learning
papers.note: LongDu self-improves long-document translation via back-translation reconstructability rewards, annotation-free.

papers.title: QueueEDIT: Structural Self-Correction for Sequential Model Editing in LLMs
papers.note: A structural mapping loss plus a queue that realigns previously edited parameters to self-correct degradation in sequential editing.

papers.title: LLMs as ASP Programmers: Self-Correction Enables Task-Agnostic Nonmonotonic Reasoning
papers.note: An automated loop where structured feedback from an ASP solver drives iterative refinement of LLM-generated programs.

papers.title: Invocation Refiner: A Plug-and-Play Module for Rectifying LLM Tool Invocations
papers.note: Takes a raw model output plus prompt and query and synthesizes corrected tool invocations.

papers.title: Teach a Reward Model to Correct Itself: Reward Guided Adversarial Failure Discovery for Robust Reward Modeling
papers.note: REFORM searches for reward-inconsistent variants and fine-tunes the reward model on a targeted augmentation of its own failures.

papers.title: Enhancing Long-Chain Reasoning Distillation through Error-Aware Self-Reflection
papers.note: ORION refines teacher chains-of-thought via error-aware self-reflection that incorporates the student's own mistakes.

papers.title: Improving LLM Code Reasoning via Semantic Equivalence Self-Play with Formal Verification
papers.note: A generator (Alice) and evaluator (Bob) train adversarially, refereed by formal proofs of program equivalence.

papers.title: OpenRubrics: Towards Scalable Synthetic Rubric Generation for Reward Modeling and LLM Alignment
papers.note: Generates synthetic rubrics at scale for reward modeling and alignment — a self-reward-style pipeline.

papers.title: Look Light, Think Heavy: What Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Can and Cannot Do
papers.note: Finds multimodal CoT handles verbal reflection but lacks deep visual introspection.

papers.title: Less Languages, Less Tokens: An Efficient Unified Logic Cross-lingual Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Framework
papers.note: UL-XCoT cuts >50% decoding cost across 18 languages while keeping competitive cross-lingual reasoning.

papers.title: Decoupling the Effect of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning: A Human Label Variation Perspective
papers.note: Reassesses the measured effect of chain-of-thought through the lens of human label variation.

papers.title: GTA: Generating Long-horizon Tasks for Web Agents at Scale
papers.note: Formalizes multi-hop web-agent task generation and releases a dynamic, reproducible benchmark.

papers.title: AgentGL: Towards Agentic Graph Learning with LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
papers.note: Equips LLM agents with graph-native tools and search-constrained thinking for multi-scale exploration via RL.

papers.title: CheckRLM: Effective Knowledge–Thought Coherence Checking in Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning
papers.note: Extracts factual claims from reasoning chains to detect and correct knowledge inconsistencies at inference.

papers.title: Contextual Relevance and Adaptive Sampling for LLM-Based Document Reranking
papers.note: TS-SetRank, an uncertainty-aware sampling reranker built on contextual relevance, lifts nDCG@10 by 15-25% on BRIGHT and 6-21% on BEIR.

papers.title: Learning from Emptiness: De-biasing Listwise Rerankers with Content-Agnostic Probability Calibration
papers.note: CapCal is a training-free content-agnostic calibration that decouples positional bias from ranking decisions in generative listwise rerankers.

papers.title: A Survey of Reasoning-Intensive Retrieval: Progress and Challenges
papers.note: Systematizes reasoning-intensive retrieval benchmarks and methods by where and how reasoning enters the pipeline.

papers.title: Adaptive Retrieval for Reasoning
papers.note: Studies when to retrieve during reasoning, proposing adaptive retrieval for large reasoning models.

papers.title: Agentic-R: Learning to Retrieve for Agentic Search
papers.note: Trains a retriever with local query-passage relevance plus global answer correctness, beating baselines on seven single- and multi-hop QA benchmarks.

papers.title: Rethinking Reasoning-Intensive Retrieval: Evaluating and Advancing Retrievers in Agentic Search Systems
papers.note: Introduces the BRIGHT-Pro benchmark and RTriever-Synth corpus, LoRA-tuning RTriever-4B for static and agentic search protocols.

papers.title: Agentic Conversational Search with Contextualized Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
papers.note: A conversational agent interleaving search and reasoning across turns, RL-trained for evolving user goals over four benchmarks.

papers.title: AgenticRAGTracer: A Hop-Aware Benchmark for Diagnosing Multi-Step Retrieval Reasoning in Agentic RAG
papers.note: A hop-aware, LLM-constructed benchmark for step-by-step diagnosis of multi-step retrieval reasoning in agentic RAG.

papers.title: PRA-RAG: Provably Robust Aggregation in Retrieval-Augmented Generation against Retrieval Corruption
papers.note: Samples retrieved-text combinations and exploits embedding geometry to derive a robust aggregate with theoretical bounds against RAG poisoning.

papers.title: ReasonEmbed: Enhanced Text Embeddings for Reasoning-Intensive Document Retrieval
papers.note: ReMixer data synthesis plus Redapter self-adaptive learning; ReasonEmbed-Qwen3-8B sets a record nDCG@10 of 38.1 on BRIGHT.

papers.title: Situated Embedding Models for Context-Aware Dense Retrieval
papers.note: SitEmb represents short chunks conditioned on a broader context window to improve dense retrieval over long documents.

papers.title: Hybrid-Vector Retrieval for Visually Rich Documents: Combining Single-Vector Efficiency and Multi-Vector Accuracy
papers.note: HEAVEN's two-stage single-then-multi-vector framework keeps 99.87% of multi-vector Recall@1 while cutting per-query compute by 99.82%.

papers.title: CLEAR: Cross-Lingual Enhancement in Retrieval via Reverse-training
papers.note: A reverse-training loss using English passages as a bridge to improve cross-lingual dense retrieval, up to 15% gains for low-resource languages.

papers.title: Reward Alignment Optimization: A Direct Point-wise Alignment Approach
papers.note: RAO uses an explicit reward model and a prefix-consistency principle for point-wise direct alignment.

papers.title: Curriculum-RLAIF: Curriculum Alignment with Reinforcement Learning from AI Feedback
papers.note: Presents AI-feedback preference data in order of increasing difficulty during alignment.

papers.title: AgentV-RL: Scaling Reward Modeling with Agentic Verifier
papers.note: Trains a verifier that interleaves tool use with internal reasoning via RL to scale reward modeling.

papers.title: HoWToBench: Holistic Evaluation for LLM's Capability in Human-level Writing using Tree of Writing
papers.note: A large Chinese writing benchmark over 12 genres showing LLM-as-judge practices are vulnerable to textual disturbance.

papers.title: LiveCultureBench: a Multi-Agent, Multi-Cultural Benchmark for LLMs in Dynamic Social Simulations
papers.note: Embeds LLMs as agents in a simulated town, scoring task completion and adherence to socio-cultural norms.

papers.title: Recovered in Translation: Efficient Pipeline for Automated Translation of Benchmarks and Datasets
papers.note: An efficient pipeline for automated benchmark/dataset translation, validated with reference-based and LLM-as-judge evaluation.

papers.title: LongSpec: Long-Context Lossless Speculative Decoding with Efficient Drafting and Verification
papers.note: Lossless speculative decoding for long-context inference with efficient drafting and verification.

papers.title: HybridKV: Hybrid KV Cache Compression for Efficient Multimodal Large Language Model Inference
papers.note: Hybrid KV-cache compression to speed up multimodal LLM inference.

papers.title: VFA: Empowering Multilingual MLLMs via Vision-Free Adaptation
papers.note: Decouples multilingual language enhancement from visual alignment by composing complementary task vectors over a shared backbone.

papers.title: LANG: Reinforcement Learning for Multilingual Reasoning with Language-Adaptive Hint Guidance
papers.note: Language-adaptive hints let RL improve multilingual reasoning without harming language consistency.

papers.title: ReLook: Vision-Grounded RL with a Multimodal LLM Critic
papers.note: A vision-aware multimodal LLM critic supplies scores and feedback inside a vision-grounded RL loop.

papers.title: "I See What You Did There": Can Large Vision-Language Models Understand Multimodal Puns?
papers.note: Probes whether large vision-language models can understand multimodal puns.

papers.title: Streaming Hallucination Detection in Long Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
papers.note: Treats hallucination in long CoT as an evolving latent state, enabling real-time streaming detection with evidence.

papers.title: LLM-Generated Text May Harm Your Retrieval! A Robust Detection Strategy for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.note: A robust detection strategy against LLM-generated text contaminating the external corpora RAG relies on.

papers.title: When Efficiency Meets Safety: A Benchmark Security Analysis of KV Cache Compression in LLMs
papers.note: Benchmarks the security implications of KV-cache compression methods in LLMs.

sources_html: ACL 2026 (San Diego, July 2–7): papers via the ACL Anthology (Main & Findings) · Paper Digest · preprints on arXiv where verified.
method_html: How I built this: I read across ACL 2026 Main and Findings and sorted a curated sample into the buckets above, weighting the self-improvement clusters because that was the throughline. This is not complete — ACL 2026 accepted ~2,300 Main plus ~2,160 Findings, and I covered a fraction. Every DOI is an ACL Anthology DOI (10.18653 prefix) confirmed against its Anthology page — none guessed — with arXiv added only where I could match a preprint by title.
footer_onepager: Every paper cited links to its ACL Anthology DOI (arXiv where a preprint was verified). Full annotated appendix follows.
footer_appendix: Prepared July 2026. A curated, verified sample of ACL 2026 (Main & Findings) — not the complete proceedings.
